summary: Audit event correlation hashmap and SIEM schema validation for missing/rewritten entries
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports apparent gaps and occasional field reordering in the audit events delivered to their Splunk HEC endpoint. They require a validated crosswalk between Redwood audit fields and the customer's SIEM schema, a per-tenant event-correlation hash map (for deterministic reconciliation), and a signed delivery manifest proving chronological delivery with resumable tokens.

Impact:
- FinNova ingested event stream contains sequence gaps for tenant finnova-123 during business hours (EUR market open).
- Customer cannot complete regulatory reconciliation for transactions due to missing audit lines.
- High priority due to regulatory deadlines; customer classified as enterprise with audit retention obligations.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted audit-export pipeline -> siem-bridge -> customer Splunk HEC (https://hec.finnovabank.internal)
- Region: eu-west-1 (prod)
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer triggers a set of API operations (model calls and management events) between 08:45-09:15 CET against tenant finnova-123.
2) Redwood audit pipeline should emit ordered events to the customer's Splunk HEC via the configured siem-bridge.
3) Customer runs a reconciliation query: count by sequence_id for the window 08:45-09:15; observed missing sequence numbers 1024..1031 and several events with corrupted 'user_id' fields (pseudonymization changed to literal 'null').
4) Customer requests signed, compressed manifest and per-tenant correlation mapping so they can reingest authoritative bundle if necessary.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged. Opened high-priority investigation and requested full event window and sample HEC receipts from customer. Escalated to SRE and serving infra.
2026-03-10 - SRE (Diego): Noted potential router backpressure and batch-compression path. Asked customer for exact ingestion timestamps and confirmed they observed gaps for seq 1024..1031.

2026-03-11 - Customer (FinNova SIEM Ops): Provided delivery receipts and recon query; asked if Redwood can provide signed manifest (gzip) plus per-event correlation hash map. Confirmed inability to re-run transactions on their side without authoritative bundle.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Marin): Running local replay of export window; initial hypothesis: small-batch coalescing combined with Kafka partition reassignment caused per-tenant events to be interleaved and some resume-token bookkeeping to drop events during an error path. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/siem-bridge/pull/1829
2026-03-12 - SRE (Diego): Deployed hotfix to siem-bridge in eu-west canary (worker-7). Monitoring for replays and delivering a signed reconciliation bundle to customer now.

2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha): Provided customer with temporary workaround: enable ordered-delivery strict mode (adds 200ms latency) and provided steps to accept a reconciliation bundle. Working on signed manifest delivery via SFTP with KMS-enveloped key.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Router batched small events and applied gzip compression which, under backpressure and partition reassignment, caused partial batch drops without proper resume-token update.
Hypothesis 2: Per-tenant correlation map generation had a race condition when the tenant's routing key moved between two workers; the sequence pointer was overwritten.

Findings: Replayed event window against internal staging; reproduce gap when partition reassignment occurs during batch finalize. The batching finalizer prematurely acknowledged to router.client, leading to 'delivered' receipts while internal resume token not advanced for that worker.

Related artifact: root-cause PR fixes batching finalizer logic and adds deterministic per-tenant correlation hashmap persistence before ack (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/siem-bridge/pull/1829).
SRE notes: No evidence of data corruption on disk; events present in internal retention store for the window. Missing downstream due to broker-to-bridge handshake race.
resolution:
Action taken:
- Deployed hotfix to siem-bridge (eu-west canary -> full eu-west roll) that fixes batching finalizer and ensures correlation-hashmap is checkpointed before ack.
- Produced a signed, gzipped reconciliation bundle (s3://redwood-eu/recon/SUP-900888/finnova-123-20260310-window.gz) with per-event HMAC (tenant-scoped) and manifest signed with Redwood KMS key. Delivered to customer's SFTP endpoint and provided exchange key material via their KMS wrapper.
- Provided temporary mitigation steps: enable 'ordered-delivery=strict' in tenant config (adds 200ms tail latency) and increase siem-bridge worker pool to prevent partition reshuffles.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem scheduled with FinNova for 2026-03-18; runbook update to include resume-token live-checks; telemetry added to detect gap patterns automatically.
- Customer asked for a field-mapping crosswalk (Redwood audit -> FinNova SIEM). Attached mapping file and mapping notes in Confluence (see related_confluence_pages).
